title: Bootstrap Readiness Marker and Dev Test Boundary
context: The active bootstrap goal requires USF to move toward controlled bootstrap readiness without starting implementation. The repository has a bootstrap readiness governance record, topology plan, semantic source-use closure ledger, machine-readable bootstrap mappings, and validate-bootstrap coverage. These decisions affect future implementation permission, proof posture, provider targets, source-use boundaries, and marker movement, so they need ADR coverage rather than only planning prose or tracker comments. USF-internal historical evidence remains informative lineage, not authority, and cannot authorise copying, path mirroring, or implementation start.
decision: USF adopts the bootstrap-readiness boundary. The future v2-bootstrap marker is a movable human-friendly marker on main and may be placed or moved only when governance, source-use treatment, topology, proof expectations, immutable proof/evidence anchors, and bootstrap validation support a later implementation attempt. The marker is not production readiness, not implementation completion, not USF-39 start authority, and not a substitute for immutable proof/evidence anchors. The initial authorised implementation attempt after bootstrap is local dev/test readiness only: dev uses in-memory providers, test uses Docker Compose OSS providers, and staging, production, live-external-provider, deployment, and production-live proof are deferred. Topology strings remain planning authority only until a signed directive and separate USF-39 start action exist.
consequences: Bootstrap readiness has rank-2 ADR coverage for its marker policy and dev/test boundary.
The bootstrap readiness governance document remains the detailed governance record, constrained by this ADR.
Validate-bootstrap must fail closed if this ADR coverage is missing or loses the core boundary markers.
The v2-bootstrap marker remains not attempted until all bootstrap blockers are resolved and validation plus immutable anchors support it.
invariants: The v2-bootstrap marker is not production readiness.
The v2-bootstrap marker is not implementation completion.
The v2-bootstrap marker is not USF-39 start authority.
USF-39 remains Backlog until a signed USF-100 directive and a separate USF-39 start action exist.
Local dev/test bootstrap readiness must not claim staging, production, live-external-provider, deployment, or production-live proof.
Future topology names are planning authority only before implementation is separately authorised.
source-lineage remains source lineage only; no runtime source, config, Compose file, migration, test, or package scaffold is copied by this decision.
permittedChanges: Strengthen validate-bootstrap checks for marker policy, ADR coverage, topology planning, source-use coverage, proof deferrals, and forbidden implementation roots.
Add or regenerate machine-readable bootstrap mappings and generated summaries where the JSON mapping remains authoritative.
Add governance records, ADRs, and validator selftests that make bootstrap readiness more falsifiable.
Move the future v2-bootstrap marker only after bootstrap blockers are resolved and repository evidence explains the move.
forbiddenDrift: Do not treat v2-bootstrap as production readiness, implementation completion, deployment readiness, or live-provider proof.
Do not use v2-bootstrap, a proof-anchor tag, a generated report, or a Linear comment as permission to start USF-39.
Do not create implementation roots or scaffold before the signed directive and separate start action.
Do not weaken dev/test provider separation by allowing in-memory providers to satisfy test Compose proof.
Do not treat source-lineage Compose, migrations, package layout, or source paths as target files to copy or mirror.
aiAlignmentRules: Agents must read this ADR before creating, moving, or relying on a bootstrap readiness marker.
Agents must preserve the distinction between local dev/test readiness and staging, production, live-external-provider, deployment, or production-live proof.
Agents must stop before creating implementation roots or scaffold from this ADR alone.
Agents must treat Linear comments as tracker context only and must verify repository artefacts and validators before claiming bootstrap readiness.
rationale: A marker is useful as a human coordination point but cannot prove correctness. Keeping the marker movable lets it follow the latest accepted candidate while immutable proof-anchor tags preserve auditability. The dev/test boundary preserves the Charter's hermetic and locally provable posture without overclaiming live-provider or production readiness. Separating the marker from USF-39 start authority prevents accidental implementation start from a bootstrap tag, CI result, generated report, or Linear comment.
description: Records the decision that the future v2-bootstrap marker is a movable bootstrap readiness marker only, and that the initial authorised implementation attempt it precedes is scoped to local dev/test readiness.
aiGuidance: Use this ADR when evaluating bootstrap readiness, marker movement, local dev/test proof boundaries, deferred production proof, or whether any future work is allowed to create implementation roots.
